questions.prompt: How do you choose and tune a garbage collector for a latency-sensitive Java service?
questions.zh: 对一个延迟敏感的 Java 服务，你怎么选择垃圾回收器、怎么调优？
outline: Define the goal first: throughput, pause time, or memory footprint
G1 is the balanced default; ZGC or Shenandoah target very short pauses
Low-pause collectors cost some throughput and need extra heap headroom
Read the GC logs before tuning: allocation rate, pause distribution, promotion
Often the real fix is in the code: allocate less, size the heap sensibly

chunks.zh: 全局停顿（所有应用线程都被暂停）

chunks.term: get promoted to the old generation

followUps: What would frequent full GCs tell you about the application?
How do you tell a GC problem apart from a memory leak?

questions.prompt: Why is a Java service often slow right after a deployment, and what can you do about it?
questions.zh: Java 服务为什么刚部署完那一阵往往比较慢？你能做些什么？
outline: A cold JVM loads classes lazily and starts by interpreting bytecode
The JIT compiles hot paths only after enough invocations
Connection pools and caches also start empty
Mitigate: send warm-up requests before readiness, shift traffic gradually
Other options: class data sharing, or native images with lower peak throughput
followUps: How does this interact with auto-scaling during a traffic spike?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a concurrency bug you've dealt with in Java. How did you find it and fix it?
questions.zh: 讲一个你处理过的 Java 并发 bug。你是怎么发现、怎么修的？
outline: Situation: intermittent wrong data or a hang that only showed under load
Reproduce with a stress test; take thread dumps if threads hang
Pin down the shared mutable state and the unsafe interleaving
Prefer confinement, immutability, or concurrent collections over adding more locks
Result: add a regression test and review similar code paths

chunks.zh: 先检查再执行（典型的竞态写法）

followUps: Why are these bugs so hard to catch in code review or unit tests?

questions.prompt: What do virtual threads change about how you write concurrent Java, and where do they not help?
questions.zh: 虚拟线程改变了你写 Java 并发代码的哪些方式？它在哪些地方帮不上忙？
outline: Threads become cheap, so plain blocking code scales without reactive frameworks
A blocked virtual thread unmounts and frees its carrier thread
Great for I/O-bound work; no gain for CPU-bound work
Do not pool them; limit concurrency with a semaphore instead
Watch for pinning on older JDKs and heavy ThreadLocal use
followUps: Would you still pick a reactive framework for a new service today?

questions.prompt: What are the common ways @Transactional silently fails to do what people expect in Spring?
questions.zh: Spring 里的 @Transactional 有哪些常见情况会悄悄失效、达不到大家的预期？
outline: It works through a proxy, so calling it from the same class bypasses it
Private and final methods cannot be intercepted
By default it rolls back on unchecked exceptions only
Catching and swallowing the exception inside the method prevents rollback
Propagation matters: REQUIRES_NEW suspends the outer transaction and uses another connection
followUps: Why is it risky to call a remote service inside a transactional method?

questions.prompt: How do you size and configure thread pools in a service that calls several downstream dependencies?
questions.zh: 一个要调用好几个下游依赖的服务，线程池的大小和配置你怎么定？
outline: CPU-bound work: roughly one thread per core
I/O-bound work: more threads, sized by wait time and downstream limits
Use bounded queues and a rejection policy; unbounded queues hide overload
Separate pools per dependency so one slow service cannot starve the rest
Measure queue time and saturation, then adjust
followUps: What should happen to a request when the pool and its queue are both full?

questions.prompt: How does the GIL affect the way you design a Python service, and what are your options for CPU-heavy work?
questions.zh: GIL 怎样影响你设计 Python 服务的方式？遇到重 CPU 的工作你有哪些办法？
outline: Only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time
Threads still help I/O-bound work because the GIL is released while waiting
For CPU-bound work: processes, native code that releases the GIL, or another service
Processes cost memory and serialization between them
Free-threaded builds exist since 3.13, but not every library supports them yet

chunks.zh: 自由线程构建版（去掉了 GIL 的 CPython）

followUps: Why did CPython have a GIL in the first place?

questions.prompt: When does asyncio make a Python service faster, and when does it make things worse?
questions.zh: asyncio 什么时候能让 Python 服务更快，什么时候反而更糟？
outline: It shines when one thread juggles many concurrent I/O waits
It does nothing for CPU-bound code, which stalls the loop
A single blocking call, such as a sync driver, freezes every request
Offload blocking or heavy work to a thread or process pool
The whole call chain must be async, which limits library choice

chunks.term: yield control back to the event loop
chunks.zh: 把控制权交还给事件循环

followUps: How would you find a blocking call hidden in an async code path?
How do you limit concurrency when fanning out thousands of requests?

questions.prompt: How do you keep a large Python codebase maintainable, given that the language is dynamically typed?
questions.zh: Python 是动态类型语言，你怎么让一个很大的 Python 代码库保持可维护？
outline: Type hints plus a checker in CI, such as mypy or pyright
Adopt gradually: strict for new modules, looser for legacy code
Hints are not enforced at runtime, so validate external data at the boundary
Tests carry more weight than in a statically typed language
Linting, formatting, and clear module boundaries do the rest

chunks.zh: 用单元测试把它覆盖到

followUps: How do you get a team to adopt type checking on a legacy codebase?

questions.prompt: A Python endpoint is too slow. How do you speed it up before you consider rewriting it in another language?
questions.zh: 一个 Python 接口太慢了。在考虑用别的语言重写之前，你会怎么给它提速？
outline: Profile first: cProfile, or a sampling profiler such as py-spy in production
Most wins are I/O or algorithmic: N+1 queries, missing caches, chatty calls
Push hot loops into built-ins, NumPy, or a native extension
Batch and parallelize I/O; cache pure results
Rewrite only the measured hot path, not the whole service

chunks.zh: 把多条查询合并成一批

followUps: At what point would you actually move that piece to Rust or Go?

questions.prompt: How do you run a Python web service in production so it uses every core and survives traffic spikes?
questions.zh: 你怎么在生产环境运行 Python Web 服务，让它既用上所有的核，又扛得住流量尖峰？
outline: Run several worker processes behind a process manager, because of the GIL
Sync workers for simple apps; async workers for many slow connections
Size workers by cores and memory, not by guesswork
Each worker holds its own connection pool: watch total database connections
Set request timeouts and restart workers gracefully on deploy

chunks.zh: Python 异步 Web 应用和服务器之间的标准接口

followUps: Where would you run long background jobs, and why not in the web workers?

questions.prompt: How would you explain ownership and borrowing to a senior engineer coming from Java or Go, and what does it buy you?
questions.zh: 面对一位写 Java 或 Go 出身的资深工程师，你会怎么解释所有权和借用？它带来了什么好处？
outline: Each value has one owner and is freed when that owner leaves scope
Borrowing: many shared references or one mutable reference, never both
The compiler enforces this, so no garbage collector is needed
It rules out use-after-free, double frees, and data races at compile time
The price: a steeper learning curve, and some designs need rethinking
followUps: What do you do when the borrow checker rejects a design you know is safe?
When do you reach for reference counting instead?

questions.prompt: How does Rust prevent data races at compile time, and which concurrency bugs can it still not prevent?
questions.zh: Rust 是怎么在编译期防住数据竞争的？还有哪些并发 bug 是它防不住的？
outline: Send and Sync mark which types may move to or be shared across threads
Shared mutation must go through a mutex, read-write lock, or atomics
A mutex owns its data, so you cannot touch it without locking
Still possible: deadlocks, logical race conditions, starvation
Message passing over channels is often simpler than shared state

chunks.zh: 标记类型能否跨线程转移、能否跨线程共享的两个 trait

followUps: What is the difference between a data race and a race condition?

questions.prompt: Why would you choose Rust for a service over Go or Java, and when would you argue against it?
questions.zh: 你为什么会给一个服务选 Rust 而不是 Go 或 Java？什么情况下你会反对用它？
outline: Strengths: predictable latency without GC pauses, low memory use, memory safety
Good fit: hot paths, proxies, data infrastructure, embedded, WebAssembly
Costs: slower onboarding, long compile times, a smaller hiring pool
For typical CRUD services, Go or Java usually ships faster
A middle path: rewrite only the performance-critical component

chunks.term: good enough for our use case
chunks.zh: 对我们的场景来说已经够用

followUps: How would you introduce Rust to a team that has never used it?

questions.prompt: How do you approach error handling in Rust, and how does it compare with exceptions in other languages?
questions.zh: 你在 Rust 里是怎么做错误处理的？和其他语言的异常机制比起来怎么样？
outline: Errors are values: Result for expected failures, panic for bugs
The question mark operator propagates errors while keeping control flow visible
Libraries expose typed errors; applications often use one catch-all with context
The compiler makes callers handle or propagate each error explicitly
Avoid unwrap on production paths; add context at each layer

chunks.zh: 表示“操作可能失败”的返回类型
直接取出里面的值，没有值就崩溃
（遇到无法恢复的错误时）崩溃

followUps: When is it acceptable to panic in a long-running service?

questions.prompt: What should a team know before building an async Rust service on a runtime like Tokio?
questions.zh: 一个团队在用 Tokio 这类运行时构建异步 Rust 服务之前，应该先了解什么？
outline: Futures are lazy state machines; nothing runs until an executor polls them
The runtime is a library you choose, not part of the language
Never block worker threads: send CPU work and sync I/O to a blocking pool
Avoid holding a standard mutex guard across an await
Cancellation means dropping the future, so design every await point for it
followUps: How do you apply backpressure when tasks are cheap to spawn?

questions.prompt: Walk me through the Node.js event loop. Why does it matter for how you write server code?
questions.zh: 给我讲讲 Node.js 的事件循环。它为什么会影响你写服务端代码的方式？
outline: One thread runs JavaScript; I/O goes to the OS or libuv's thread pool
Phases: timers, pending callbacks, poll, check, close callbacks
nextTick and promise callbacks run between callbacks, before the loop moves on
Any long synchronous work delays every other request
So keep handlers short and keep I/O asynchronous
followUps: Which operations actually use the libuv thread pool, and which don't?

questions.prompt: A Node.js service's latency spikes under load while CPU sits at one full core. How do you diagnose and fix it?
questions.zh: 一个 Node.js 服务一上负载延迟就飙升，而 CPU 正好占满一个核。你怎么诊断、怎么解决？
outline: Suspect a blocked event loop; measure event loop delay to confirm
Capture a CPU profile or flame graph to find the synchronous hot spot
Typical culprits: huge JSON payloads, sync crypto or file calls, catastrophic regex backtracking
Fix: chunk the work, move it to worker threads, or to another service
Add event loop delay to dashboards and alerts
followUps: When are worker threads the wrong tool for this?

questions.prompt: Node runs your JavaScript on a single thread. How do you scale a Node service across cores and machines?
questions.zh: Node 只在一个线程上跑你的 JavaScript。你怎么让 Node 服务扩展到多个核、多台机器？
outline: One process per core: the cluster module, or more containers behind a load balancer
Keep processes stateless; put sessions and caches in external stores
Worker threads are for CPU-heavy tasks, not for scaling request handling
WebSockets need sticky sessions or a shared pub/sub layer
On SIGTERM: stop accepting connections, finish in-flight requests, then exit

chunks.zh: 每个 CPU 核 fork 一个工作进程

followUps: What breaks if an in-memory cache lives inside each process?

questions.prompt: How do streams and backpressure work in Node, and when have they mattered to you?
questions.zh: Node 里的流和背压是怎么工作的？它们在什么场合对你很重要？
outline: Streams handle data in chunks instead of loading everything into memory
Backpressure: a slow destination tells the source to pause
Manually: stop when write returns false, resume on the drain event
Prefer pipeline over pipe: it forwards errors and cleans up
It matters for large uploads, exports, proxies, and log processing

chunks.term: buffer the whole file in memory
chunks.zh: 把整个文件缓冲进内存
把（一个流）接到（另一个流）上

followUps: What happens to memory if a producer ignores backpressure?

questions.prompt: How should a Node.js service deal with unhandled promise rejections and uncaught exceptions in production?
questions.zh: 生产环境里的 Node.js 服务应该怎么对待未处理的 Promise 拒绝和未捕获的异常？
outline: Separate operational errors from programmer bugs
Handle operational errors per request: validate, catch, return a proper status
Since Node 15, an unhandled rejection crashes the process by default
On an uncaught exception, log, stop accepting traffic, and restart: state may be corrupt
Rely on an orchestrator and multiple instances to absorb restarts

chunks.zh: 未处理的 Promise 拒绝

followUps: Why is it dangerous to catch everything and keep the process running?

questions.prompt: How do you decide which language or runtime to use for a new backend service?
questions.zh: 一个新的后端服务该用哪种语言或运行时，你是怎么决定的？
outline: Start from the workload: I/O-bound, CPU-bound, latency-sensitive, memory-constrained
Team skills and hiring usually outweigh benchmark differences
Ecosystem: libraries, tooling, cloud SDKs, operational maturity
Limit how many languages the organization has to support
Prototype the riskiest part before committing

chunks.zh: 考虑到当时的限制条件

followUps: Tell me about a language choice you later regretted.
How many languages is too many for one engineering organization?

questions.prompt: Memory usage of a production service grows steadily until the process gets killed. How do you track down the leak?
questions.zh: 一个线上服务的内存持续上涨，直到进程被杀掉。你怎么把泄漏点找出来？
outline: Confirm it is a real leak: memory keeps rising even after GC
Compare heap dumps or snapshots taken some time apart
Find what is growing and what keeps it reachable
Common causes: unbounded caches, listeners never removed, growing maps, unclosed resources
Mitigate first if needed: restart or roll back, then fix and add monitoring
followUps: What if the heap looks stable but the process memory still grows?

questions.prompt: An API's p99 latency has doubled since last week, but the average looks fine. How do you investigate?
questions.zh: 一个接口的 p99 延迟比上周翻了一倍，但平均值看着正常。你怎么排查？
outline: Check what changed: deploys, traffic mix, data size, dependencies
Tail latency points at outliers: GC pauses, lock contention, slow queries, retries
Use tracing to see where the slow requests spend their time
Compare slow and fast requests: payload, tenant, shard, instance
Form a hypothesis, test it, and confirm the fix on the same metric
followUps: Why is the average a poor signal for user-facing latency?

questions.prompt: What principles do you follow when designing an API that other teams will depend on for years?
questions.zh: 设计一个别的团队要依赖很多年的 API 时，你遵循哪些原则？
outline: Design from the consumers' use cases, not from your database tables
Make it hard to misuse: consistent naming, pagination, a clear error model
Make writes idempotent so clients can retry safely
Evolve additively; bump the version only for breaking changes
Document the contract; deprecate with notice and real usage data
followUps: How do you retire an endpoint that some clients still call?
When would you pick gRPC or GraphQL over REST?

questions.prompt: Walk me through how you'd build a system that answers questions from a large internal document set.
questions.zh: 讲讲你会怎么搭一个能根据大量内部文档回答问题的系统。
outline: Chunk the documents, embed them, store in a vector database
Retrieve top candidates by semantic similarity, rerank, then generate with citations
Documents change — indexing must be incremental
Evaluate with a golden set before tuning anything
Grounding beats model size for factual answers
followUps: How do you keep answers from going stale when the documents change daily?
Keyword search or vector search — or both? Why?

questions.prompt: LLMs hallucinate. How do you keep that under control in a production feature?
questions.zh: 大模型会产生幻觉。在生产功能里你怎么控制它？
outline: Ground answers in retrieved sources and require citations
Constrain the output format; reject non-conforming output
Human in the loop for anything consequential
Guardrails screen outputs for sensitive data
Measure the hallucination rate on an evaluation set — vibes are not a metric

chunks.zh: 护栏（AI 输出的安全约束）

followUps: Give me an example of a hallucination your users actually hit.
When is a wrong answer acceptable, and who decides?

questions.prompt: When would you fine-tune a model instead of using retrieval?
questions.zh: 什么情况下你会选微调而不是用检索？
outline: Retrieval teaches facts; fine-tuning teaches format and style
Facts that change weekly belong in retrieval
Fine-tune when the behavior must change, not the knowledge
Fine-tuning costs more to run and to keep fresh
Most products need RAG first, fine-tuning later if at all
followUps: Have you ever fine-tuned? What data did you use?
How would you combine both in one system?

questions.prompt: How do you know whether a change to your AI feature made it better or worse?
questions.zh: 你怎么判断对 AI 功能的一次改动到底是变好还是变差了？
outline: Build a golden evaluation set from real cases, written by domain experts
Run every prompt or model change against it before shipping
Track precision and recall for retrieval separately from answer quality
Watch for model drift — rerun evals on a schedule
Public benchmarks don't know your users
followUps: How big does an evaluation set need to be to trust it?
What do you do when human reviewers disagree with each other?

questions.prompt: Your AI feature works, but it's slow and expensive. What do you do?
questions.zh: 你的 AI 功能能用，但又慢又贵。你怎么办？
outline: Measure first: tokens per request, time to first token, cost per request
Cache repeated prompts and results
Route easy requests to a smaller model
Stream responses so perceived latency drops
Cut context — most prompts carry dead weight
followUps: Which lever gave you the biggest win?
How do you stop cost controls from hurting answer quality?
